channel.title: HAT MI Daily - Macro and Industries
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: US third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to an annualised 4.3% from 3.4% on AI-related investment and consumer spending, while the PCE price index rose 3.8% year on year in October and the Fed's Beige Book says input costs are outpacing selling prices.
item.description:
The upward revision reflected stronger business investment driven by the AI build-out and software, as well as consumer spending, Axios reports; growth in the second quarter was 2.2%. Personal income rose 0.7% in October, while inflation-adjusted consumer spending stalled and the saving rate rose to 4.1% from 3.6% in September, according to Axios. Core PCE inflation was 3.3% year on year, against 3.2% expected, MarketScreener reports. In the Beige Book, the Federal Reserve reports slight to moderate growth in most of the US in recent weeks, with eight districts reporting growth and four unchanged activity; contacts reported sustained cost pressure from energy, transportation, health care, insurance and tariff-related expenses, but competition and customers' price sensitivity limited how much they could pass on, MarketScreener and The Economic Times report. The Beige Book says business investment led by AI remained strong while consumer spending was flat, as households were increasingly stretched and trading down. The Fed is broadly expected to raise its policy rate, now 3.75%–4.00%, by at least a quarter point at its 8–9 December meeting, though market-based expectations have eased amid the stock selloff, The Economic Times reports. The reports differ on September's PCE rate (3.6% in Axios, a revised 3.7% in Handelsblatt).

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

US third-quarter growth was revised up on AI-related investment and consumer spending, but real consumer spending stalled in October and the Beige Book describes households as increasingly stretched, and inflation is high enough that a rate rise is broadly expected. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, costs rising faster than selling prices squeeze margins in manufacturing and distribution, and higher rates weigh on housing and durable goods. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, AI-related building and electronics support demand in data centres and electronics assembly, while flat consumer spending and an expected rate rise could weigh on consumer goods, cars and home improvement. Points that may be worth considering include the Fed decision on 9 December, and whether the new tariff proposals add to the tariff-related costs the Beige Book reports.

Axios | MarketScreener | Handelsblatt | MarketScreener | The Economic Times

item.title: China's car manufacturing industry had receivables of almost CNY 3 trillion at end-September, collection periods of up to 100 days against 66 in 2020, and profits down about 23% year on year in January–September, CPCA's Cui Dongshu says.
item.description:
According to Cui Dongshu, secretary-general of the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA), as reported by Lianhe Zaobao, the industry's profit margin on sales was only 3.3% in the first nine months, against 9% in 2014 and below the 6.7% the report gives for downstream industry as a whole. The report does not say how the receivables are split between carmakers and suppliers, or how they compare with a year earlier.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

China's car manufacturing industry is waiting longer to be paid and earning less, which points to a sector under financial strain. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, longer payment periods in a supply chain mean that suppliers finance their customers, which tightens working capital for smaller suppliers first. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, if carmakers pass the strain up the chain, material suppliers to Chinese carmakers and their parts makers could face longer payment terms and price pressure, which affects the attractiveness of this business even where volumes grow. Points that may be worth considering include whether the collection period shortens in the coming quarters, and whether profits recover in the fourth quarter.

Lianhe Zaobao

item.title: India's cabinet has approved an INR 110 billion scheme over eight years to raise domestic production of construction and infrastructure equipment and reduce dependence on imports, after China restricted exports of some heavy machines.
item.description:
The scheme, approved on 25 November, has a two-year period for setting up manufacturing facilities followed by five years of incentive payments, The Economic Times reports. Eligible equipment makers and component manufacturers will receive sales-linked incentives of 13% to 8% on incremental sales over five years, and a grant of up to INR 3.75 billion will support a dedicated testing facility. The reports describe the scheme as running for eight years but give phases of two and five years, and do not explain the difference. It covers equipment such as tunnel boring machines, hydraulic excavators, ship-to-shore cranes and off-highway trucks, according to Business Standard and The Times of India. China's restrictions on exports of certain heavy equipment, including tunnel boring machines, walking excavators and select dredging components, took effect on 18 November, The Economic Times reports. MarketScreener puts the scheme at USD 1.2 billion and reports Information Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw as saying it will attract INR 210 billion of investment and lead to INR 225 billion of import substitution. India's construction equipment market was about INR 975 billion in the 2024/25 fiscal year, and the government expects it to more than double to about INR 2.28 trillion by 2029/30, driven by investment in roads, ports, housing and other infrastructure, Business Standard reports. The reports do not give the current share of imports from China.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

India is using incentives to build a domestic supply of construction machinery, after China imposed export controls on key machinery, while the government expects the equipment market to more than double by 2029/30. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a sales-linked incentive rewards local assembly and local components, so it tends to pull a supplier base of parts and materials into the country over several years. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, heavy equipment manufacturing uses structural bonding, sealing and threadlocking in cabins, engines and hydraulic systems, so new production in India may create local demand for these materials, as the infrastructure projects themselves do for construction applications. Points that may be worth considering include which manufacturers apply for the scheme, and whether China's equipment export restrictions are widened or eased.

Business Standard | The Economic Times | The Economic Times | The Times of India | MarketScreener

item.title: The UK government has confirmed plans for a General Safety Requirement, a new safety duty for construction products not covered by a designated standard or a technical assessment, which it estimates covers about 63% of all construction products.
item.description:
Products already regulated under the construction products regulations will not also fall under the General Safety Requirement, the National Federation of Roofing Contractors (NFRC) reports. The report does not give a start date, how compliance will be shown or enforced, or which product groups make up the 63%.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The UK plans a new safety duty for construction products that have no designated standard or technical assessment, which the government estimates at about 63% of all construction products. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, a general safety duty usually requires manufacturers to show that a product is safe in its intended use, which adds documentation and testing for products sold without a designated standard. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, construction bonding and sealing products that are not covered by a designated standard could fall under the new duty, depending on how the product scope is defined. Points that may be worth considering include the timetable for the new duty, and what evidence of safety it will require from manufacturers and importers.

NFRC

item.title: UK electric car registrations reached 503,805 so far in 2026, 30.4% more than a year earlier, but SMMT expects a 27.2% market share for the year against the 33% target of the ZEV mandate and warns that the UK risks losing car investment.
item.description:
In October, electric car registrations were 32.7% higher than a year earlier and took 32% of the UK new-car market, according to Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT) figures reported by The Independent. SMMT says the UK risks losing automotive investment unless the government removes high industrial costs, looming EU trade barriers and what it calls unsustainable EV regulation, and that manufacturers spent more than GBP 10 billion on discounts in 2024 and 2025 to stimulate demand for electric vehicles. On SMMT's account, the Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) mandate targets continue to outpace demand, adding to depreciation and pressure on consumer finance costs and used-car values. Xinhua reports that the mandate requires all new cars and vans to be zero-emission by 2035. Separately, Ireland, which holds the EU's rotating presidency, has proposed that the UK could be included in the EU's planned "Made in Europe" scheme, formally the Industrial Accelerator Act, which aims to protect EU manufacturing with a particular focus on China and the car industry, BBC News reports; inclusion would depend on the UK granting the EU access to its subsidy and procurement schemes. The reports do not give total new-car registrations, UK car production, or the size of the investment SMMT says is at risk.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Electric car sales in the UK are growing fast but, on SMMT's forecast, not fast enough to meet the mandate, and the industry links this to its investment decisions. SMMT's statement is an industry position, not a measured outcome. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, heavy discounting to meet a sales quota supports volumes in the short term but reduces the margins that fund new models and factories. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, a rising electric share points to more battery, thermal and structural bonding per car, while any loss of UK vehicle investment would reduce local demand for automotive assembly materials. Points that may be worth considering include whether the UK government changes the mandate, and whether UK-built cars are included in the EU's "Made in Europe" rules.

The Independent | SMMT | Xinhua | BBC News

item.title: The US Trade Representative has found the manufacturing overcapacity practices of 14 economies, including China, the EU, Japan and India, actionable under Section 301 and proposed additional duties, with 15% for the EU and 20% for China.
item.description:
On 25 November, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer determined that the acts, policies and practices of China, the EU, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan and India relating to structural excess capacity in manufacturing are unreasonable and burden or restrict US commerce, USTR says. For the EU, USTR proposes additional duties on all products, except as provided in the notice, and will take public comments and hold a hearing. POLITICO reports proposed rates of 20% for China, 18% for Cambodia, Indonesia, Thailand, Bangladesh and Malaysia, and 15% for the EU, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland to stay within agreed ceilings, and 10% for Singapore; Vietnam could get 20% if a trade deal still under negotiation is reached and up to 35% without one, and India 17% with a deal and up to 25% without. Hong Kong Economic Times reports that China's rate could double to 40% if US–China talks break down, and that the EU, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland's 15% could rise to at most 20%. The proposed rates for the EU, Taiwan, Japan and South Korea are net of both existing Section 301 duties and most-favoured-nation tariffs, while India's rate is adjusted only for existing Section 301 tariffs, The Hindu Business Line reports. Semiconductors, cars, steel and aluminium, already covered by Section 232 tariffs, are excluded, as are some energy and food products, Chinatimes reports, citing Yahoo Finance. A senior US official said new tariffs could take effect no earlier than January, Süddeutsche Zeitung reports; Taiwan's trade working group says public consultation runs to 5 January 2027 and hearings start on 25 January, Commercial Times reports. USTR has not made determinations for Mexico or Norway at this time, MarketScreener reports, and separately proposed new tariffs on Brazilian imports, including a 10% tariff on finished aircraft, saying Brazil continues to export significant amounts of out-of-quota sugar and finished aircraft that are exempt from earlier tariffs, Xinhua reports. The European Commission rejected the claim that Europe fuels overcapacity, POLITICO reports; at a routine press conference on 25 November, China's foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun called so-called overcapacity "a false proposition", China Economic Net reports; Japan called the proposal "regrettable", Anadolu Agency reports, and Singapore said it was "very disappointed", CNA reports. Global stock markets fell on 25 November in a broad selloff after the tariff proposal, with US technology shares leading declines amid concerns about inflation and a hawkish Federal Reserve, CNA reports; reports differ on how far US indices recovered by the close, with Yahoo reporting a partial recovery in the afternoon. The reports do not give product exclusion lists for most economies or the trade value covered.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

This is a formal US finding against 14 economies that Chinatimes describes as major trading partners, followed by proposed duties, on all products except those exempted in the case of the EU, with rates for the EU, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland set to stay within agreed ceilings and higher fallback rates for some economies where deals are not reached. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, the comment period and hearings leave room for exclusions, and the gap between the capped and fallback rates gives Washington leverage in talks with India, Vietnam, South Korea and China. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, duties on all EU products, except those the notice exempts, would reach chemical and material exports from the EU to the US, and duties on the Asian economies could do the same depending on their product scope, as well as finished goods containing bonded components, while the exclusion of cars and semiconductors, along with steel and aluminium, removes two large bonded-goods categories from this round. Points that may be worth considering include which products the final notices exclude, whether China's rate stays at 20% or rises towards 40% if US–China talks break down, and whether the EU responds with measures of its own.

USTR | USTR | POLITICO | HKET | The Hindu Business Line | Chinatimes | Süddeutsche Zeitung | Commercial Times | MarketScreener | Xinhua | POLITICO | China Economic Net | Anadolu Agency | CNA | CNA | Yahoo

item.title: Orders of the VDMA Electrical Automation association rose 11% in real terms in January–September 2026 from a year earlier and its turnover rose 8%, and the association's chair expects turnover to grow about 8% for the full year.
item.description:
The forecast comes from Jessica Bethune, chair of the board of VDMA Electrical Automation and vice-president industrial and process automation at Schneider Electric, VDMA reports. The report does not give export and domestic shares, a breakdown by product, or quarterly figures.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The association's orders rose faster in real terms than its turnover in the first nine months, though the report does not say whether the turnover figure is price-adjusted, so the two are not directly comparable. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, automation equipment is bought by manufacturers investing in production, so this contrasts with the fall in German equipment investment in the third quarter reported in another insight in this alert, and the two measure different things over different periods: one association's January–September orders against a year earlier, and national investment in the third quarter against the second. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, electrical automation products such as drives, controls and sensors use electronic bonding, potting and protective materials. Points that may be worth considering include whether orders hold up in the fourth quarter, and whether the growth comes from German or foreign customers.

VDMA

item.title: Germany's GDP grew 0.1% in the third quarter from the second, below the preliminary 0.2%, Destatis data show, with exports down 1%, including cars and car parts, chemical products and metals, and equipment investment down 3.5%.
item.description:
Handelsblatt reports that consumer spending also developed weakly, with private households holding back on food and on energy products such as fuel; Süddeutsche Zeitung writes that consumer spending grew only slightly amid higher inflation. Construction investment shrank slightly in the quarter, Süddeutsche Zeitung reports. Economists remain optimistic for the current year, Handelsblatt writes, not least because of government spending of many billions of euros on defence and infrastructure. The Federal Statistical Office's preliminary estimate, published at the end of October, had put third-quarter growth at 0.2%, Handelsblatt reported at the time. Investment in machinery, devices and vehicles fell 3.5%, Süddeutsche Zeitung reports. The reports do not give the year-on-year growth rate or the size of the fall in chemical exports.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The German economy barely grew in the third quarter, less than first estimated, and the weakness includes areas linked to industry, such as exports of cars, chemicals and metals and investment in machinery and vehicles, as well as consumer spending. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a fall in equipment investment means fewer orders for machinery and vehicle makers in the following quarters, while public spending on defence and infrastructure supports construction and some manufacturing with a delay. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, lower car exports and machinery investment in Germany could reduce demand in automotive and industrial assembly, and weaker chemical exports point to a harder export market for German chemical producers. Points that may be worth considering include whether the end of the slump that Süddeutsche Zeitung reports is expected soon shows in the fourth-quarter figures, and how quickly public infrastructure and defence spending turns into orders.

Handelsblatt | Süddeutsche Zeitung | Handelsblatt

item.title: New orders in Germany's main construction industry fell 16.1% in value in September from August, with civil engineering down 20% and building construction 10.6%, though third-quarter orders were 2.5% above the previous three months, Destatis data show.
item.description:
In July–September, civil engineering received 5.9% more orders than in the previous three months and building construction 1.6% fewer, according to the Federal Statistical Office figures reported by Handelsblatt and Süddeutsche Zeitung. Compared with September 2025, order intake fell 6.5% in real terms (1.6% in nominal terms), while turnover rose 11.4% in nominal terms to EUR 12.1 billion (5.8% in real terms), according to Handelsblatt and Süddeutsche Zeitung, which say significant price increases contributed; Wallstreet:online gives the same growth rates for companies with 20 or more employees. Employment rose 2% to about 553,000. Felix Pakleppa, chief executive of the construction federation ZDB, said the record increase in August had had little significance: as soon as large orders fail to materialise, order intake slips back into negative territory, Wallstreet:online reports. Wallstreet:online also reports that residential construction is still not getting off the ground and building construction orders remain below the previous year's level, while in civil engineering the first additional orders from the special fund are visible. The reports do not give separate figures for residential construction or the size of the large orders behind the August result.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

German construction orders are volatile from month to month, and the quarter shows a modest gain driven by civil engineering, while building-construction orders remain below the previous year's level and, on ZDB's account, residential construction is still not getting off the ground. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, turnover that rises about twice as fast in nominal as in real terms points to a large price component, and orders lead construction activity by several months. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, building construction and renovation draw more on flooring, tile, insulation and sealing applications than civil engineering does, so continued weakness in building orders matters more for demand than the third-quarter rise in civil engineering orders. Points that may be worth considering include whether infrastructure orders from the special fund build into a steady flow, and whether residential orders show any turn in the coming months.

Handelsblatt | Süddeutsche Zeitung | Wallstreet:online
